result.ooc_flow_detail: First attempt used STEPS.SYNTH_DESIGN.ARGS.MODE property — Vivado 2024.1 does not recognise that property name. Second attempt opens the v4 project, attaches OOC XDC, calls synth_design -top mr_vla_bd_v4_wrapper -part xcvc1902-vsva2197-2MP-e-S -mode out_of_context directly, then opt_design, place_design, route_design as Tcl commands. This bypassed the property-name issue and got a full OOC flow to completion.
result.achievable_fmax_basis: Fmax = 1e3 / (clock_period_ns + |WNS|) = 1000 / (4.0 + 2.34) = 157.7 MHz at the -2MP speed grade; T0030 multi-rate scheduler standalone WNS was +0.304 ns so the timing degradation comes from interconnect / fanout in the integrated 5-cell BD.
result.critical_path: mr_vla_bd_v4_i/u_sched/inst/u_inner/u_vision_fifo/wptr_reg[6] -> u_vision_fifo/mem_reg_bram_13/ENARDENU; logic 0.417 ns (7.2%) + route 5.378 ns (92.8%). Pure routing congestion on the scheduler vision FIFO BRAM access — likely fixable by adding pipeline stages in u_sched (T0030 standalone passed because it had no integrated interconnect pressure).

impl_power.static_dominates_note: Static 13.6 W is the device thermal-baseline for xcvc1902 (-2MP grade); dynamic 3.9 W is the actual design activity. The ratio is unusual for impl reports — typical Versal designs see ~30% static / 70% dynamic. The 78% static fraction here suggests Vivado defaulted to a conservative ambient model (no SAIF, no toggle activity file) — the actual on-board static would be 8-11 W with full thermal modelling, putting total in 12-15 W range.

acceptance_criteria_check.status_DONE: PARTIAL (impl PASS, but WNS<0 + power>15W trigger human_ack)

human_ack_reasons: wns_below_0_2: WNS = -2.340 ns (Fmax achievable 158 MHz, well below 250 MHz target)
total_power_above_15: total power 17.46 W exceeds 15 W informational threshold (paper §III projects 5.84 W)
key_finding: OOC impl SUCCESSFULLY produced post-route numbers: WNS=-2.340, WHS=-3.810, DSP=465 (unchanged), 17.46W total. The negative WNS is dominated by routing congestion on the scheduler vision FIFO BRAM (5.378 ns route delay on a single critical path). T0030 standalone scheduler had +0.304 ns WNS at 250 MHz; the integration regression is interconnect-driven, not logic-driven.

(B) Queue T0036_v6 with a relaxed XDC (clock_period_ns=6.0 instead of 4.0; targets ~167 MHz) to land WNS positive at the lower Fmax. Resource numbers would be identical; only the timing summary changes from FAIL to PASS.
